newsitem.title: UK: Seasonal food to put upward pressure on UK May RPI.
newsitem.headline: Seasonal food to put upward pressure on UK May RPI.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics said on Thursday seasonal food prices were likely to exert upward pressure on UK inflation in May.
"Seasonal food prices tend to rise in May and the poor fruit crop in Europe due to frost damage means fruit prices in particular will probably rise," an ONS statistician said.
This may be partly offset by lower prices for domestic lamb.
Within the non-seasonal food category, the world wide rise in pork and bacon prices was expected to continue.

Within housing costs, most lenders put up their mortgage rates following the base rate rise this month. Rates rises of between 0.3 and 0.35 percent took effect for new borrowers immediately but would have minimal effect on the May all-items RPI, the ONS said. Existing borrowers would start to pay the new rates from June 1.
Within motoring costs, the ONS said it expected used car prices to continue to fall in May.
